title: Business Analytics Consulting and Solution Design

offerings.format_notes: Five sessions; attendance mandatory.

description: A case-based course on designing effective business analytics solutions, emphasizing that framing the problem correctly is the most critical part of any analytics project. Students learn to translate business needs into solvable analytical problems, avoid common data-science failure modes, and plan modeling, prescriptive analytics, and deployment.
topics: translating business needs into analytical problems
workload_basis: Four assignments (mostly 1-page reviews plus a group capstone presentation review), readings, no exams.
grading: Four assignments (75 pts) plus attendance (25 pts); no final exam.
notes: Unexcused absence costs half a letter grade; students review live capstone presentations in class.

title: Business Analytics in Marketing, Finance & Operations

offerings.format_notes: Three modules taught by three different professors, each 1/3 of the grade.

description: A three-module intensive course introducing analytics applications in marketing, finance, and operations, each taught by a different professor. Topics span customer value and advertising measurement, time value of money and portfolio concepts, and process analysis with capacity and inventory fundamentals.
skills: evaluating advertising effectiveness and causal claims
financial decision-making with NPV and TVM
prerequisites: There are no prerequisites to this course.
workload_basis: Per-module assessments: quizzes and exercises (marketing), group homework plus take-home and oral exams (finance), homework plus written and oral exam (operations).
grading: Three module grades, each 1/3 of the total; marketing module curved; oral exams in finance and operations modules.
notes: Paper quizzes with no devices; oral exams in two modules; preparation before class essential.

title: Collecting and Analyzing Large Data

offerings.format_notes: 8am Tuesday meetings; several flipped classes.

description: An introduction to tools and frameworks for collecting and analyzing large datasets to drive strategic business decisions. Covers the full analytics project cycle — scoping, data collection (web scraping, APIs, experiments), exploratory analysis, predictive modeling, and presenting findings — with a team project consulting for a real organization.
skills: collecting data via scraping, APIs, and experiments
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of algebra and introductory probability. Familiarity with common business concepts such as revenue, cost, profit, conversion, retention, and customer value.
workload_basis: Midterm and final exams, individual assignments, team project for a real organization, participation, flipped-class pre-work.
grading: 35% final exam, 20% midterm, 20% team project, 10% assignments, 15% participation.
notes: Team project consults for an actual business; GenAI encouraged but students must explain all submitted code.

title: Business Analytics
description: A foundations course in business analytics focused on using data, statistical models, and quantitative methods to make decisions under uncertainty. Covers decision analysis, statistical inference, simulation, regression, and optimization with hands-on programming in R and Python, applied through six team case studies.
workload_basis: Seven homework assignments, six team case write-ups, participation, plus 3-hour midterm and final exams.
grading: 35% final exam, 25% midterm, 15% case write-ups, 10% homework, 15% participation.
notes: Six group case write-ups in study groups; open-book but strictly individual exams; peer evaluations factor into participation.

title: Business Analytics Capstone
description: The MSBA capstone: teams solve a real business analytics problem for an external sponsor company, covering the full project cycle from scoping and a client-approved charter through data preparation, analysis, and final recommendations. Emphasis on project management, stakeholder communication, and professional delivery.
skills: presenting to technical and nontechnical audiences
prerequisites: Taken in the final quarter; applies techniques from the whole program (requires MGTA 451, 452, 453).
workload_basis: Explicitly ~12 hours/week: weekly client and advisor meetings, biweekly peer surveys, mid-term and final presentations with individual exams.
grading: 25% professionalism, 25% teamwork (peer surveys), 15% output quality, 15% communication, 20% individual understanding.
notes: External company sponsor; mandatory weekly client and faculty meetings; strict data handling rules.

title: AI-Assisted Customer Analytics
description: Core course on customer analytics (no syllabus PDF was available; summary based on the Rady program website). Typically covers analytics for customer acquisition, retention and churn, customer lifetime value, and targeting/response models.
workload_basis: Unknown — syllabus not available.
grading: Unknown — syllabus not available.
notes: Core per the Rady MSBA website; details limited because no syllabus was in the source folder.

title: Machine Learning: Learning Algorithms

offerings.format_notes: Historically a Fall course; it is not on the Fall 2026 CSE graduate list, so confirm on the CSE tentative offerings page.

description: Algorithms for supervised and unsupervised learning from data: maximum likelihood, log- linear models including logistic regression, nearest neighbor methods, kernel methods, decision trees, ensemble methods, optimization, topic models, neural networks, and backpropagation.
prerequisites: Graduate standing; strong math (linear algebra, probability) strongly advised.
workload_basis: Graduate CSE problem sets and exams; mathematically demanding.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Pre-approved MSBA elective (listed by Rady as CSE 250B, renumbered to 251A). Historically offered in Fall only, and not listed for Fall 2026. Check the CSE department's tentative graduate course offerings page before you plan around it — CSE majors have priority and seats go as space permits.
also_known_as_note: renumbered; Rady's electives page still lists it as CSE 250B

title: Deep Learning

offerings.format_notes: Offered most Winters (and some Springs); confirm on the CSE tentative offerings page.
Offered some Springs; confirm on the CSE tentative offerings page.

description: Fundamentals of deep neural networks at the graduate level: multi-layer perceptrons, backpropagation, automatic differentiation, convolutional networks, recurrent networks, transformers, and advanced deep learning topics.
skills: building and training deep neural networks
prerequisites: CSE 251A (or equivalent ML background).
workload_basis: Graduate CSE programming projects; mathematically demanding.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Successor to the old 'Neural Networks for Pattern Recognition' (CSE 253) on Rady's pre-approved list. Runs in Winter, sometimes Spring — never Fall in recent years. Check the CSE department's tentative graduate course offerings page before you plan around it — CSE majors have priority and seats go as space permits.
also_known_as_note: successor to CSE 253 on Rady's pre-approved list

title: Statistical Learning

offerings.format_notes: Rarely offered — last ran Winter 2023 and Spring 2021. Confirm on the CSE tentative offerings page.

description: Learning algorithms based on statistics: minimum-variance unbiased estimators, maximum likelihood estimation, likelihood ratio tests, resampling methods, linear logistic regression, feature selection, regularization, dimensionality reduction, manifold detection.
prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor; strong statistics background advised.
workload_basis: Graduate CSE theory-oriented coursework.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: NOT on Rady's pre-approved MSBA elective list (that list carries CSE 250B/251A, CSE 253/251B and CSE 256 only) — taking it would need MSBA advising approval. Rarely offered: last ran Winter 2023. CSE majors have priority; enroll as space permits.

title: Statistical Natural Language Processing

offerings.format_notes: Ran in Winter in 2024 and 2025; confirm on the CSE tentative offerings page.

description: Modern statistical approaches to natural language processing: part-of-speech tagging, word sense disambiguation, parsing, Markov and hidden Markov models, and probabilistic context-free grammars.
skills: building NLP pipelines from statistical foundations
prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
workload_basis: Graduate CSE problem sets and projects.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Pre-approved MSBA elective; deeper theoretical complement to MGTA 415. Scheduled for Fall 2026 (Nakashole); has also run in Winter. Check the CSE department's tentative graduate course offerings page before you plan around it — CSE majors have priority and seats go as space permits.

title: Business Analytics for Managers
description: This course provides a foundation in business analytics for students of all backgrounds, covering statistics and uncertainty, decision analysis, and optimization. Students process data, build mathematical models to improve decision making, and use statistics to gain business insights. The course uses the Radiant tool, a no-code data processing and visualization tool within the R environment.
skills: using simulation to predict complex outcomes
communicating analytical findings in managerial memos
reading and interpreting business analytics reports
workload_basis: Graded work includes seven weekly assignments, six group case memos, a take-home midterm project with presentation, a final exam, and class participation.
grading: The syllabus lists weights of 40% for assignments, 25% for the final exam, 20% for the midterm project and presentation, 15% for individual homework assignments, and 15% for group case assignments.

title: Business Analytics for Managers
description: This course introduces students to the foundations of business analytics. It teaches managers how to be comfortable exploring their data, how to create and use models to make better decisions in complex settings, and how to use statistics to better understand their business setting. The course covers uncertainty, decision analysis, and optimization.
skills: communicating analytical results to non-technical audiences
workload_basis: Eight weekly assignments, five case quizzes with writeups, and a final project with report and presentation.
grading: Final project writeup 40%, final project presentation 5%, individual case quizzes and writeups 25%, individual homework assignment quizzes 30%.

title: Accounting
description: This course examines fundamental accounting concepts and principles, with the goal of helping students become informed users of financial statements rather than training them as accountants. Classes include interactive lectures, discussions, and short cases involving corporate financial statements to illustrate accounting concepts and explore companies' disclosure strategies.
skills: asking management questions about financial statements
understanding international differences in financial statements
analyzing how transactions flow into financial statements
using accounting information for business decisions
prerequisites: None.
workload_basis: Graded work consists of weekly Connect quizzes, a midterm, a final exam, and in-class participation, with optional homework and self-study problems.
grading: Grading is based on graded online homework (15%), class participation (10%), the mid-quarter exam (25%), and the final exam (50%).

title: Managerial Economics
description: This course introduces the use of microeconomics in managerial decision-making, examining how market structure, competitive and regulatory constraints, and the structure of information affect a firm's optimal strategy. Topics include supply and demand analysis, price discrimination, contractual relationships, and asymmetric information, with an emphasis on marginal analysis. The course uses lectures, case discussions, in-class work sessions, and homework to apply economic principles to business problems.
skills: applying marginal analysis to profit maximization
using price elasticity to guide pricing decisions
designing pricing strategies such as versioning, bundling, and non-linear pricing
deriving optimal supply decisions for competitive firms
analyzing the effects of regulations on market behavior
developing strategic responses to market entry threats
designing incentive schemes to address conflicts of interest
workload_basis: Graded work includes two exams, group and individual homework assignments, reading questions, and in-class work sessions.
grading: Graded on two exams, homework assignments, and class participation, using the formula of the two that yields the higher grade.

title: Managerial Economics
description: An introduction to the use of microeconomics in managerial decision-making, examining how market structure, competitive and regulatory constraints, and information affect a firm's optimal strategy. Topics include supply and demand, price discrimination, contractual relationships, and asymmetric information, with emphasis on marginal analysis. The course combines in-person lectures, asynchronous videos, online simulations, and class discussions.
skills: applying marginal analysis to profit maximization
using price elasticity to guide pricing decisions
designing pricing strategies such as versioning, bundling, and non-linear pricing
deriving optimal supply recommendations in competitive markets
assessing the effects of regulations on market behavior and welfare
applying strategic thinking to pricing and capacity decisions
designing effective incentive schemes considering conflicts of interest
workload_basis: Weekly reading questions and homework problems, class participation including moblab simulations, and a final exam.
grading: Final exam 35%, homework 45%, and class participation 20%.

title: Leadership, Ethics, and Team Management
description: Students learn and develop key leadership skills through case analysis, articles, in- class exercises, discussion, and written assignments. The course covers self-awareness, personality, emotional intelligence, ethics, team dynamics, conflict negotiation, and power and influence, with an emphasis on applying research-based knowledge to real managerial challenges.
skills: applying leadership research to managerial challenges
assessing personal leadership strengths and weaknesses
setting and pursuing leadership development goals
analyzing team dynamics using course frameworks
applying research-based knowledge to leadership challenges
assessing personal leadership strengths and development areas
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, a personal development plan, and a team paper, alongside weekly readings, cases, online modules, and team activities.
grading: Grading is 40% participation (assessed by peers and professor), 35% Personal Development Plan, and 25% Team Paper.

title: Competitive Strategy
description: This course focuses on strategic decision making by companies in competitive markets. The approach combines applied economic theory with empirical examples to develop competitive advantage and game theory frameworks. Classes consist of both lecture and discussion of applications, including case studies.
workload_basis: Graded work includes three group case write-ups, a closed-book in-class exam, and a final group project with written analyses and presentation.
grading: Grading is based on group case write-ups (30%), an in-class exam (35%), and a final group project (35%).

title: Competitive Strategy
description: This course focuses on strategic decision making by companies in competitive markets. The approach combines applied economic theory with empirical examples to develop competitive advantage and game theory frameworks. Classes consist of lecture and discussion of applications, including case studies.
skills: identifying sources of profit within and across industries
directing company growth, innovation, and responses to changing markets
analyzing strategic interactions between competing and complementary companies
shaping industry competition to a firm's advantage
workload_basis: Graded work includes participation, five group case write-ups, a take-home exam, and a final group project.
grading: Grading is based on participation (20%), group case write-ups (20%), a take-home exam (30%), and a final group project (30%).

title: New Venture Design
description: This course teaches students to transform user needs, strategic intent, and technological innovation into viable new products, services, and ventures. It introduces design thinking and a hybrid top-down/bottom-up approach, using case studies, readings, practical exercises, peer feedback, and a final team project to develop and pitch a compelling business concept.
skills: analyzing factors that focus a company's innovation efforts
synthesizing research to uncover user insights
constructing compelling positioning for new offerings
crafting and presenting a compelling business case
evaluating and critiquing the work of others
workload_basis: Graded work includes teamwork, class participation, practical exercises and submissions, and a final team project presentation and report.
grading: The course grade is based on teamwork (10%), class participation (20%), practical exercises and submissions (30%), and the team project presentation (40%).

title: New Venture Design
description: This course teaches students to transform user needs, strategic intent, and technological innovation into viable new lines of business or ventures. It introduces design thinking and a hybrid top-down/bottom-up approach, with online modules, in-person sessions, practical exercises, and a team project culminating in a concept pitch.
skills: synthesizing user needs into actionable insights
critiquing and evaluating the work of others
workload_basis: Graded work includes teamwork, class participation, practical exercises, and a team project presentation/report.
grading: Course grade is based on teamwork (10%), class participation (20%), practical exercises (30%), and a team project presentation (40%).

title: Rady Action Project
description: Students work in teams on a real consulting project sponsored by a business client, applying management techniques to scope, analyze, and solve a business problem. The course emphasizes client communication, team dynamics, and professional deliverables, culminating in a final presentation and executive summary.
skills: clarifying client problems through interviews and questioning
structuring business problems using frameworks like fishbone diagrams
workload_basis: Estimated 11-12 hours per week across research, problem solving, status reports, work plans, presentations, and final deliverables.
grading: Graded on team deliverables (project charter, work plans, client status reports, executive summary), midterm and final presentations, discussion posts, case study, and professionalism/participation.

title: New Venture Development
description: An action-based practicum focused on assessing the viability of venture ideas and developing them into sustainable new enterprises, whether in entrepreneurial, intrapreneurial, or social enterprise contexts. Students learn customer discovery, lean business model development, and market, financial, and risk evaluation through lectures, case studies, team projects, presentations, and guest speakers.
skills: projecting market demand and profit potential
writing executive summaries and business plans
workload_basis: Graded on class participation (15%), homework and exams (20%), and a team New Venture Project (65%), with a fast-paced, project-heavy format.
grading: Students are evaluated on class participation (15%), homework and exams (20%), and the New Venture Project (65%).

title: Current Business Law Issues
description: An overview of current issues in business law, covering how legal rules shape business decisions, contracts, risk management, and dispute resolution. Students learn substantive areas of business law through lectures, case discussions, and practical group exercises.
topics: legal system and sources of authority
skills: evaluating legal risk in business decisions
workload_basis: Three group projects, a midterm, a final exam, and weekly class participation.
grading: Midterm 25%, group work/presentation 25%, class participation 25%, and final exam 25%.

title: Negotiation
description: This course develops negotiation skills through a series of simulations and debriefings. Students negotiate in pairs or groups, then analyze outcomes through class discussion, covering value claiming, value creation, and multiparty negotiation. It addresses common problems managers and professionals face, emphasizing strategy, psychology, and cognitive biases in negotiation.
skills: creating joint gains in integrative negotiations
managing psychological biases at the bargaining table
preparing for and executing negotiation exercises
reflecting on negotiation outcomes and personal effectiveness
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation and case write-ups, two 600-word journals, and a final project, plus weekly negotiation exercises.
grading: Grading is based on class participation (50%) and a final (50%), with no late assignments accepted.

title: The Board of Directors, the CEO, & Corporate Governance
description: This course introduces the legal, political, and practical relationships that govern how businesses operate at the highest level of management. It covers the evolution of the modern corporation, the structure and duties of boards of directors, conflicts among boards, CEOs, and shareholders, and how to research and evaluate corporate governance practices. The hybrid format combines in-person sessions, video lectures, readings, discussions, and a team proxy research project.
skills: understanding board duties and legal obligations
workload_basis: Weekly readings and videos, four written assignments, a team proxy research project and paper, and weekly discussion participation.
grading: Graded on four written assignments, weekly discussion participation, and a team proxy research project and paper.

title: Managerial Judgment and Decision Making
description: This course examines how people make judgments and decisions, focusing on uncertainty and variability, and how to design effective decision processes. It then shifts to building, protecting, and exerting influence to implement decisions and achieve goals. The course is taught through exercises, case discussions, and lectures.
topics: decision making via models and algorithms
skills: applying behavioral insights to business strategy
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, a take-home midterm, a final project, and multiple pre-class surveys and assignments.
grading: Grading is based on class participation (25%), a take-home midterm (35%), and a final project (40%).

title: Biotechnology Industry, Structure & Strategy
description: This course examines the biotechnology industry as a business, focusing on running a biotechnology company rather than starting one. It combines discussion and lecture with real-world case studies, covering major functional areas including discovery, development, manufacturing, regulation, marketing, and sales, as well as strategy, financing, licensing, intellectual property, reimbursement, and organizational behavior. Students take leadership roles in case discussions and complete an in-depth company analysis.
skills: analyzing biotechnology company business models and competitive positioning
evaluating strategic options and trade-offs under uncertainty
leading case discussions and defending recommendations
conducting primary research through interviews and public sources
assessing financial impact of strategic decisions
developing actionable recommendations from a senior executive perspective
workload_basis: The course requires heavy preparation: class participation and online assignments (35%), leading case discussions, and a three-installment Company Assignment paper (65%) with required interviews.
grading: Class participation and online assignments count 35% and the Company Assignment paper counts 65%; final grades reflect absolute performance and relative standing, with no exams.

title: Power and Politics
description: This course examines organizational power and politics, teaching students to understand power dynamics, develop influence skills, and build a personal path to power. It uses readings, case discussions, in-class exercises, reflection papers, and a final strategic plan, with a hybrid format of video lectures, Canvas discussions, and in-person sessions.
skills: assessing sources of power and influence
developing a personal strategic plan for power
workload_basis: Graded work includes weekly discussion participation, short reflection papers, and a 12-page final paper with an informational interview.
grading: Course grade is 37% participation (34% class discussion, 3% surveys), 18% reflection papers, and 45% final paper.

title: Managing Healthcare and Life Sciences
description: This seminar-style course explores the business of healthcare and life sciences from a U.S. perspective, with comparisons to other countries. Students examine the roles, motivations, and interdependencies of patients, providers, payers, government, and industry, and then focus on innovation and disruption in the field. Teaching relies on lectures, case studies, and open discussion.
skills: conducting financial analysis of healthcare ventures
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, a healthcare executive interview, an innovation team project, reflection memos, and a midterm exam.
grading: Grading is based on class participation (20%), a healthcare executive interview (10%), an innovation team project (25%), reflection memos (20%), and a midterm exam (25%).

title: Topics in Organizational Behavior: Leadership in Practice: Coaching and Inclusion
description: This highly participatory course equips managers with skills to communicate strategically in person and virtually, across team meetings, boardrooms, public forums, and investor pitches. Through lectures, demonstrations, creative exercises, improvisations, peer feedback, and individual coaching, students develop and rehearse presentations for contexts such as attracting talent, gaining stakeholder buy-in, pitching clients, and motivating teams.
skills: analyzing an organization's competitive arena and context
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, case leadership, a team consulting project with a 10-15 page report and presentation, and an individual presentation.
grading: Grade is based on class engagement (10%), individual homework (15%), a partner coaching exam and reflection (15%), and final projects including a de-biasing project and leadership vision (50%); attendance at all weekend sessions is required to pass.

title: Spreadsheet Modeling
description: This course focuses on managerial modeling approaches used to make better business decisions, covering optimization and decision making under uncertainty. Students translate problems into mathematical models solved with Microsoft Excel, then analyze and interpret results. The course includes deterministic models such as linear and integer optimization, followed by Monte Carlo simulation with random variables.
skills: translating managerial decisions into mathematical models
modeling uncertainty with random variable distributions
interpreting model outputs for business decisions
workload_basis: Six group assignments, a midterm, a final exam, and class participation.
grading: Grading is based on six group assignments (42%), class participation (8%), a midterm (20%), and a final exam (30%).

title: Topics in Operations & Technology: Global Supply Chain Management - New Approaches
description: This course takes an end-to-end systems perspective on global supply chains, focusing on how supply chain decisions affect a company's financial statements, cash flow, working capital, and shareholder value. It covers operational finance, traditional and newer supply chain financing methods, fintech and blockchain-enabled trade finance, and the costs, benefits, and risks involved. Teaching combines lectures, data-driven case studies, in-class discussion, and team research projects, delivered over Zoom.
skills: identifying genai opportunities in business processes
analyzing supply chain risk and resilience
evaluating supply chain trade-offs and decisions
articulating supply chain issues to executives and policymakers
prerequisites: This is a Master’s Level Program.
workload_basis: Graded work includes a full-quarter group project (50%), individual assignments (20%), and class participation (30%), with weekly sessions and project milestones.
grading: The course is graded on a team case assignment (25%), a team research assignment deck/presentation (35%), class attendance/participation (10%), and an individual final exam/deliverable (30%), with final grades also considering ranking among students.

title: AI and Disruptive Technology Strategy

offerings.format_notes: Scheduled as the MGT 451R section (course equivalent — no credit for both). Confirm the section on the UCSD Schedule of Classes.
Scheduled as the MGT 451R section (course equivalent — no credit for both). Confirm the section on the UCSD Schedule of Classes.

description: MBA elective on strategy for technology-driven businesses: how firms create and capture value from innovation, platform and ecosystem dynamics, and competitive strategy in technology markets.
prerequisites: MBA program admission or consent of instructor.
workload_basis: MBA case-discussion course.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Pre-approved MSBA elective (MBA course — enrollment by consent). Listed on Rady's electives page under its former title, Technology and Innovation Strategy; the UCSD catalog now titles it AI and Disruptive Technology Strategy. The scheduled section is MGT 451R (Fall 2026, Winter 2027), a course equivalent — no credit for both. Highly relevant for product management careers.
also_known_as_note: MGT 271 is the MBA-numbered equivalent; no credit for both

title: AI & Disruptive Technology Strategy
description: This course explores how AI and disruptive technologies redefine businesses and enable industry transformation. It covers frameworks such as S-curves and the Technology- Organization-Ecosystem (TOE) theory to analyze technology change, competitive advantage, and digital transformation. The course is mostly online and asynchronous, with lecture videos, weekly quizzes, case discussions, and group presentations.
skills: discriminating between trends and fads using s-curves and toe theory
making strategic decisions on technologies, products, markets, and investments
evaluating the transformative impact of ai across industries
assessing social, ethical, and legal implications of ai
proposing innovative ai initiatives or startups
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes and discussions, plus one group case presentation and one group term project presentation.
grading: Graded on weekly quizzes (30%), participation (30%), a group case presentation (20%), and a group term project presentation (20%), with no midterm or final exams.

title: New Product Development
description: This course provides a broad framework for new product development, emphasizing a user- centered approach and empathic design to understand what people want. Students learn qualitative research techniques, generative methods, and prototyping to define and communicate a product vision. The course uses case studies, readings, multimedia, and practical exercises, culminating in a team project.
topics: organizational issues in new product development
skills: conducting user research to uncover needs
translating research data into product insights
applying generative techniques to refine product concepts
building prototypes to communicate product vision
analyzing cases and readings for new product development decisions
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, practical exercises, and a team project with presentation and report.
grading: Class participation counts 30%, practical exercises 30%, and team project presentation 40%.

title: New Product Development
description: This course explores new product development from a user-centered perspective, emphasizing empathic design and qualitative research to understand customer needs. It covers the NPD framework, prototyping, and visualization techniques, and includes a team project where students design a product with both physical and digital components. The course uses a hybrid format with online modules and in-person sessions.
skills: using generative techniques for product definition
prerequisites: MGT 412/MGT 412R: New Venture Design
workload_basis: Graded work includes participation, practical exercises, and a team project presentation.
grading: 30% participation, 30% practical exercises, and 40% team project presentation.

title: Supply Chain Management
description: Supply chain management involves the flows of materials and information among all firms that contribute value to a product, from raw materials to end customers. The course integrates marketing, logistics, and operations management perspectives, and covers how data analytics and digital transformation can make supply chains more flexible, resilient, and transparent. Students use conceptual frameworks to analyze supply chain issues including distribution, forecasting, inventory, and risk management.
skills: identifying elements of a strong brand
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, a quiz, three case write-ups, two homework assignments, and a take-home final exam.
grading: Grades are based on class participation (10%), a quiz (10%), case write-ups (30%), homework assignments (20%), and a take-home final exam (30%).

title: Customer Analytics and (Generative) AI
description: This hands-on course uses real-world data to equip students with the tools and conceptual understanding needed to leverage customer analytics for immediate business value. It covers the evolving data landscape, the role of generative AI in analytics, and how to move from traditional segmentation to individual-level customer connections at scale. Instruction blends in-person sessions, online videos and readings, individual and group assignments, and exercises.
skills: evaluating model performance with lift and gains charts
using generative ai for data analysis
workload_basis: Graded work includes individual and group assignments, case analyses, exercises, and a peer evaluation form.

title: Experiments in Organizations
description: Businesses increasingly use experimentation in pricing, marketing, employee incentives, and consumer behavior. This course teaches students how to design and run randomized experiments in organizations, incorporating insights from behavioral economics. It combines lectures with workshopping to develop experimental proposals and pilot studies.
skills: incorporating behavioral economics insights into interventions
presenting experimental proposals to decision makers
workload_basis: Graded work includes weekly response surveys, an article presentation, a pilot study with data analysis, and a final experimental proposal with presentations and peer feedback.
grading: Grading is based on participation and response surveys (25%), article presentation and peer feedback (25%), pilot study and peer feedback (25%), and the final experimental proposal and peer feedback (25%).

title: Topics in Innovation - Bringing a Product to the U.S. Market
description: This course focuses on contextual growth and entrepreneurship, exploring options across the risk/reward spectrum such as acquisition entrepreneurship, side-hustles, scalable entrepreneurship, corporate entrepreneurship, and angel/venture investing. Students develop a Personal Entrepreneurial Plan and/or business pitch deck, engage in a multi- week venture simulation, and learn through real-life case studies and guest speakers from the life-sciences and technology industries.
skills: synthesizing course material in an exam
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, four case analysis quizzes, a professional growth sweetspot reflection, a team venture simulation debrief or pitch presentation, and an individual exam.
grading: The final grade is based on class engagement (20%), case analysis quizzes (20%), a professional growth sweetspot reflection (20%), an exam (20%), and a team simulation debrief or pitch presentation (20%).

title: Behavioral Economics and Market Design
description: This course explores the intersection of behavioral economics, decision-making, and market design. Students learn how psychological, cognitive, and emotional factors influence individual and firm decision-making, and apply these insights to design more efficient and equitable markets, policies, and business strategies. The course includes case studies, group work, and a final poster presentation pitch.
skills: analyzing cognitive biases and their impact on decision-making
applying behavioral economics principles to business problems
developing and presenting a pitch for a behavioral problem
workload_basis: Graded work includes participation, individual assignments, and a final group project pitch with poster presentation.
grading: Participation is 25%, individual assignments are 25%, and the final group project is 50%.

title: Data Science with Artificial Intelligence
description: This course teaches business students to manage AI for data analytics, starting from zero coding experience. Students learn R programming and 'vibe coding'—using natural language to direct AI agents to scrape data, run causal inference, and build production- ready analyses. The course progresses from understanding AI to collaborating with, managing, and promoting AI agents, culminating in building custom GPTs.
skills: scraping and analyzing social media data
prerequisites: None
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes, multiple individual and group homework assignments, and a multi-part final project.

title: Consumer Behavior

offerings.format_notes: Scheduled as the MGT 477R section (course equivalent — no credit for both). Confirm the section on the UCSD Schedule of Classes.
Scheduled as the MGT 477R section (course equivalent — no credit for both). Confirm the section on the UCSD Schedule of Classes.

description: MBA elective on how consumers perceive, decide, and buy: psychological foundations of consumer decision-making and their implications for marketing strategy, brand, and product design.
skills: translating consumer psychology into marketing and product decisions
prerequisites: MBA program admission or consent of instructor.
workload_basis: MBA case-discussion course.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Pre-approved MSBA elective (MBA course — enrollment by consent). Runs in Spring: the scheduled section is MGT 477R (SP26, SP27), a course equivalent — no credit for both. Pairs well with experiments (MGTA 458) for PM/marketing careers.
also_known_as_note: MGT 203 is the MBA-numbered equivalent; no credit for both

title: Consumer Behavior
description: This course provides frameworks, methodology, and knowledge to help students gain customer insight and connect that insight to marketing strategy and implementation. It covers qualitative methods, consumer culture, lifestyle, needs, customer journeys, and innovation adoption, with a focus on designing and interpreting marketing research. The course blends in-person sessions with online asynchronous materials, case discussions, lectures, and group projects.
skills: applying behavioral insights to marketing strategy
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation (30%), three individual assignments (25%), and three group assignments (45%), with multiple case readings and group projects.
grading: Grading is based on class participation (20% online, 10% in-person), individual assignments (15%, 2%, 8%), and group assignments (15% each, totaling 45%).

title: Brand Management
description: A case-based MBA course examining brands as co-creations of consumers and marketers, and the strategic tasks required of brand managers. Topics include brand equity, architecture, extensions, storytelling, licensing, crisis management, and luxury branding. Emphasis is on applying frameworks to real-world cases through discussion and participation.
skills: applying brand management frameworks to cases
integrating social media into branding strategy
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes, participation/assignments, and a final exam with individual and group components.
grading: Grading is based on weekly quizzes (48%), assignments and participation (16%), a final exam (30%), and SET/extra credit (6%), using a standard letter grade scale.

title: Fundamentals of Real Estate Analysis
description: This course applies corporate finance and investment principles to real estate markets, covering private and public markets, debt and equity, and commercial real estate assets. It emphasizes a value-based framework for real estate decisions, including valuation, mortgage underwriting, development, and leasing, while also addressing historical trends such as segregation and redlining. Instruction combines asynchronous lectures, in-person sessions, quizzes, and team presentations.
skills: analyzing leverage and mortgage effects on returns
evaluating real estate investment risk and return
measuring returns and using price indices
assessing demand and supply drivers of real estate value
understanding historical public policy impacts on urban patterns
workload_basis: Three closed-book long quizzes, a team presentation, and class participation determine the grade.
grading: Grading is based on three long quizzes (60%), a team presentation (30%), and class participation (10%).

title: Valuation
description: Valuation is the science and art of assigning a fair market value to an asset. The course develops in-depth knowledge of the determinants of firm value and why short-term stock price is likely to deviate from long-term value, covering discounted cash flow valuation, equity risk models, relative valuation, and real options. It uses case studies and spreadsheet models and ties valuation to the state of the macroeconomy.
topics: valuation of start-ups and young firms
skills: calculating cash flow to equity, cash flow to the firm, and free cash flow
evaluating risk characteristics and developing appropriate discount rates
choosing the right valuation model for a particular firm
appraising special situations such as start-ups and distressed firms
building discounted cash flow and relative valuation models
prerequisites: Core MBA courses: MGT 403, 404, 405, 406, 407, 408, 409, 410, 413, familiarity with Microsoft Excel.
workload_basis: Eight quizzes, a team project with presentation and report, case readings, and class participation.
grading: Team project is worth 20 points, quizzes are worth 70 points with the lowest quiz grade dropped, and class participation is worth 10 points.

title: Applied Market Research
description: This course covers planning, implementing, and analyzing market research, with an emphasis on hands-on application. Students move through the full research arc, from formulating a research question and conducting exploratory qualitative work to designing surveys and using adaptive conjoint analysis to quantify trade-offs. The course also focuses on synthesizing multi-method results and presenting findings effectively.
prerequisites: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.
workload_basis: The syllabus states each week is designed to fill approximately 12 hours, with graded work including individual assignments, team weekly assignments with peer reviews, and a final presentation.
grading: Grading is based on individual assignments (10%), team weekly assignments and peer reviews (40%), and a final presentation (50%), with team grades adjusted by peer evaluations of contribution.

title: Mergers, Acquisitions, and Corporate Restructurings
description: This course explores major corporate reorganizations including acquisitions, divestitures, and restructurings, and how firms use them to create shareholder value in response to competitive challenges and opportunities. It provides a framework for analyzing transactions through in-depth case studies, covering valuation, accounting, taxation, governance, cross-border deals, and buyouts.
topics: history and economic role of corporate acquisitions
skills: mastering the language and process of m&a and restructuring
identifying problems and opportunities in corporate reorganizations
analyzing transactions rigorously and understanding drivers of success or failure
forming educated opinions about proposed deals
applying accounting and taxation concepts to acquisitions and restructurings
understanding the regulatory framework of corporate acquisitions
presenting a case analysis of an m&a transaction
prerequisites: Knowledge of the concepts of finance developed in MGT 408, basic familiarity with Microsoft Excel.
workload_basis: Seven quizzes, a team research presentation, and class participation, with substantial case reading and a team project.
grading: Grading is based on quizzes (72 points, best six of seven), a team research presentation (18 points), and class participation (10 points).

title: Investments
description: A survey of the investment landscape covering asset classes, securities, and modern portfolio theory. Students use an Interactive Brokers trading account to track self- managed portfolios and then dive into security selection. The course aims to develop and analyze investment strategies that maximize returns and minimize risks for medium and long-term horizons.
skills: analyzing asset class returns and risks
conducting security selection and due diligence
performing fixed income analysis including duration and convexity
valuing equities using dcf and relative valuation
using derivatives for hedging and speculation
evaluating market efficiency and behavioral biases
workload_basis: Homework and quizzes, credit and equity projects, a final team report, and participation.
grading: Course grade is based on homework and quizzes (20%), credit and equity projects (30%), final team report or exam (30%), and participation (20%).

title: Financial Risk Management
description: This course introduces fundamental principles of risk management, applying modern financial techniques to assess and mitigate various types of risk using financial strategies and instruments. It covers key risk measures such as Value-at-Risk and Cash- Flow-at-Risk, derivatives for hedging, and real-world cases, with a strong quantitative component and emphasis on practical application.
skills: applying risk measures to project selection and performance evaluation
managing exchange rate, commodity, and interest rate risk
evaluating regulatory and credit risk frameworks
prerequisites: Core Finance
workload_basis: Three group case studies, individual quizzes, class participation, and an individual take-home final exam.
grading: Case studies 40%, quizzes 10%, class participation 10%, and final examination 40%.

title: New Venture Finance
description: This course helps managers make better investment and financing decisions in entrepreneurial settings, covering the full lifecycle of a new venture from deal sourcing and evaluation to term sheets, fund performance, and exits. It uses a hybrid model combining asynchronous online lectures and readings with synchronous, interactive case discussions and exercises.
skills: calculating startup valuations using the vc method
workload_basis: Graded work includes participation, quizzes/assignments, a midterm, and a final exam.
grading: Participation is 20%, quizzes/assignments 20%, midterm 30%, and final 30%.

title: Topics in Finance: International Finance
description: This course introduces machine learning and AI methodologies for financial applications, focusing on alternative and unstructured data sources. Students learn to apply econometric and ML tools to extract patterns that inform portfolio choices, systematic strategies, and trading signals. The course emphasizes hands-on programming, industry guest speakers, and a group project mimicking quant research pods.
skills: utilizing capital budgeting techniques in an international setting
assessing transaction, translation, and competitive currency risks
designing hedging strategies with forwards, options, and swaps
managing political risk in cross-border transactions
explaining interactions between fiscal policy, monetary policy, trade, and currency fluctuations
applying machine learning to financial data
workload_basis: Grading is based on a group project (50%), a project presentation (25%), and class participation (25%).
grading: Grading is based on class participation (10%), two group assignments (60%), and one group case submission (30%).

title: Data-Driven Communications

offerings.format_notes: Five highly participatory lab sessions.

description: A highly participatory lab course on presenting data through clear, compelling storytelling. Students use actor-training techniques to strengthen delivery, vocal range, and audience connection, building weekly presentations that culminate in a final storytelling-with-data presentation.
workload_basis: Weekly readings, presentation prep, peer feedback and reflections, plus a final project presentation over five sessions.
grading: 40% engagement/participation/peer feedback, 60% individual and group assignments; no exams.
notes: Attendance essentially mandatory (participatory lab); AI-generated work explicitly prohibited.

title: AI-Assisted Math & Programming for Business Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Compressed two-week intensive with daily class and lab sessions.

description: An intensive summer gateway course that builds math, statistics, and programming foundations for the MSBA in a Generative AI era. Students implement core concepts (mean, variance, A/B testing, clustering) from scratch in Python without external libraries, practice test-driven development, and learn to collaborate with AI tools on business problems.
prerequisites: Assigned DataCamp coursework, self-paced online math & stats bootcamp, recommended OpenIntro Statistics review (Ch. 1-5).
workload_basis: Compressed two-week format: daily sessions, skills test, programming cases, probability problem sets, written and oral final exam.
grading: Pass/fail (S/U) based on written and oral final exam; individual assignments and participation count significantly.
notes: All work individual; students must be able to explain every line of code in person; some assignments allow GenAI, some forbid it.
units_note: Catalog lists 2-4; pre-term intensive graded S/U, treated as required prep (not counted toward the 50 units).

title: Analyzing Unstructured Data (NLP & LLM Applications)

offerings.format_notes: Five sessions; taught by an industry data science VP.

description: An applied course on natural language processing and large language models for business. Briefly reviews classical NLP (preprocessing, embeddings) then moves into transformers, prompt engineering, RAG, LLM agents, and multimodal models, with one comprehensive group project building an AI-driven business application.
skills: applying NLP to business text data
prerequisites: Math and basic statistics, Python programming, basic supervised machine learning.
workload_basis: One comprehensive group project with midterm and final presentations, plus quizzes and labs; no exams.
grading: 30% attendance/quizzes/labs, 30% midterm project presentation, 40% final project presentation.
notes: Team project (3-4 students); strict attendance policy; heavy GenAI use expected and rewarded.

title: Supply Chain Analytics
description: Links supply chain theory with data analytics applications: mapping a company's supply chain, managing demand and supply-side uncertainty, and communicating improvement strategies. Spans classical methods (newsvendor, forecasting, inventory) through last- mile delivery, sustainability, and revenue management, with hands-on Python and Excel work.
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes, 5-7 homework assignments, group case write-up, group final project; no exams.
grading: 10% participation, 10% case write-up, 25% homework, 25% quizzes, 30% final project; no exams.
notes: Quizzes every class (lowest dropped); group case and group final project; AI tool use encouraged.

title: Business Intelligence Systems

offerings.format_notes: Weeks 6-10 (second half of quarter); Tableau-focused, no Snowflake.
Weeks 6-10; adds Snowflake cloud data warehousing alongside Tableau.

description: A hands-on, project-based course on turning high-volume data from disparate systems into actionable insights through interactive dashboards. The Fall section centers on Tableau and Tableau Prep; the Spring section adds the Snowflake Data Cloud for scalable storage, SQL/ELT, and data modeling. Culminates in a team dashboard project and presentation.
workload_basis: One multi-part team project (design doc, prep workflow, dashboards, presentation, final doc) plus quizzes over 5 weeks; no exams.
grading: Mostly project-based (presentation + deliverables ~85%), quizzes ~5-10%.
notes: Half-quarter course (weeks 6-10). Portfolio-ready team project; GenAI use expected but logic must be explainable.

title: Experiments for Business Analytics (Experiments in Firms)
description: Covers how businesses and policymakers use randomized experiments in pricing, marketing, employee incentives, and consumer behavior, incorporating behavioral economics into experimental interventions. Groups develop a business question, design a randomized experiment, run a pilot study, and present results.
workload_basis: Midterm (35%), two small individual assignments, milestone-based group pilot project with presentation.
grading: 15% participation, 10% individual assignments, 35% midterm, 40% group final project.
notes: Quarter-long teams of 2-4 with peer evaluation; strict no-AI policy for assignments and exams.

title: Managerial Judgment and Decision Making

offerings.format_notes: Thursday/Friday intensive blocks.
Six 4-hour Saturday morning sessions (8am-12pm) — good for students preferring a weekend/compressed schedule.

description: A two-part course on making better decisions and getting them implemented. Part one examines judgment under uncertainty (heuristics, biases, noise, group decisions, models vs. intuition, risk taking); part two covers building influence through coalitions, networks, and persuasion, ending with a personal action plan.
workload_basis: Heavy reading and case prep, frequent pre-class surveys/assignments, take-home midterm, open-format final project; no coding.
grading: 25% participation, 35% take-home midterm, 40% final project (Personal Action Plan).
notes: Discussion- and case-heavy with graded participation; two sections with identical content but different schedules; AI use allowed with disclosure.

title: Business Analytics Project Management

offerings.format_notes: Five sessions; pop-quiz every class.

description: Focuses on leading analytics projects: designing and planning work, coordinating dispersed teams, managing senior-management expectations, and managing risk. Covers stage-gate processes, critical path and PERT scheduling, resource allocation, real options, modularity, and agile development, anchored by a team case building a Python simulation of uncertain project durations.
skills: Monte Carlo simulation of project durations in Python
workload_basis: Pop-quiz every class, two individual quizzes, two-part team case with code and design doc, final exam worth 40%.
grading: 10% pop-quizzes, 30% team case (write-up + code), 40% final exam, 20% individual quizzes.
notes: Attendance effectively mandatory (missed class forfeits pop-quiz credit); team deliverable is a reusable Jupyter Monte-Carlo tool.

title: Web Mining and Recommender Systems (cross-listed CSE 258)
description: Current methods for data mining and predictive analytics with emphasis on real-world datasets and building working systems: recommender systems, web mining, and putting current machine learning research into practice.
prerequisites: Comfortable programming and machine learning fundamentals.
workload_basis: Programming-assignment and project driven CSE-style course.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Cross-listed with CSE 258 — counts as an MGTA elective (not against the 16-unit non-MGTA cap). CSE 258 has run every Fall since 2017 (Winter sections occasionally); the MSBA section is scheduled for Fall 2026. Taught in the CSE department style: expect substantial coding.

title: Fraud Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Fully online (no physical classroom); no exams.

description: Teaches building statistical and machine learning models to detect fraud: raw data analysis and cleaning, expert feature engineering, algorithm selection, and model evaluation. Real-world supervised and unsupervised problems include credit card transaction fraud, NY property tax anomalies, and application identity fraud.
topics: ML algorithms (trees, random forests, boosting, neural nets)
skills: end-to-end fraud detection pipelines in Python
cleaning and profiling large dirty datasets
prerequisites: Good background in math and statistics and working ability in Python.
workload_basis: Ten individual homework assignments with weekly deadlines, including three substantial report-based projects on real datasets.
grading: 10 homeworks (130 pts) plus participation (10 pts); curved (roughly half As).
notes: Taught online by an industry fraud-analytics practitioner; real datasets; no exams; curved grading.

title: SQL and ETL

offerings.format_notes: Mixed remote and in-person Saturday morning sessions; proctored skills test each class; advanced SQL through window functions and recursive CTEs; ETL case with Python + Snowflake.
Quiz-heavy format with proctored in-class quizzes; ETL case project.

description: Foundational course on working with data in relational databases using SQL and on building Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) workflows. Progresses from database concepts through complex querying (joins, subqueries, aggregations, CTEs, window functions) to ETL pipelines producing analysis-ready datasets, ending with an ETL case project.
skills: loading and transforming data in Snowflake
workload_basis: Proctored SQL quizzes/skills tests most sessions plus a group ETL project.
grading: Mostly proctored quizzes/tests (70-90%) plus ETL group project.
notes: Highly test-based grading; strong foundation for any data-engineering-leaning role.

title: Scalable Analytics
description: Performing analytics at scale on big data: computer systems and parallelism fundamentals, distributed processing with Hadoop and Spark, and cloud-based analytics on AWS. Hands-on weekly programming assignments in PySpark and Python, including machine learning with Spark MLlib, Amazon EMR, and SageMaker.
skills: building analytics models on big data
using cloud platforms for scalable analytics
prerequisites: Solid Python programming experience required (all assignments in PySpark/Python).
workload_basis: A programming assignment every week (80% of grade) plus four strict closed-book quizzes.
grading: 80% weekly programming assignments, 20% quizzes.
notes: Strictly individual assignments; closed-book quizzes with no AI/notes; strong signal for data engineering roles.
units_note: Catalog lists 2; weekly programming assignments make it feel bigger.

title: Pricing Analytics
description: A heavily quantitative, hands-on course treating pricing as the intersection of economics, strategy, and data science. Covers value pricing, demand estimation from surveys, experiments, and field data, price discrimination, bundling, and subscriptions, applied to real managerial data with a team pricing-strategy project for an actual product or business.
skills: estimating demand and setting optimal prices
prerequisites: Statistics and regression knowledge expected; no prior economics needed.
workload_basis: Five short homeworks, in-class midterm, and a substantial team project worth half the grade.
grading: 10% homework, 10% attendance/participation, 30% midterm, 50% team project.
notes: Team project (2-4 people) with week-10 presentations; human-in-the-loop AI use encouraged.

title: Special Topics: AI & Prescriptive Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Mandatory attendance: missing more than 3 classes results in an F.

description: An integrated introduction to AI and prescriptive analytics: first half covers deep learning (MLPs, CNNs, RNNs/LSTMs, transformers, NLP, LLMs) plus interpretability and bias; second half covers discrete-event simulation, mixed-integer programming, and dynamic programming for data-driven decisions. Hands-on Python labs apply methods to operations, finance, and healthcare.
workload_basis: Five homework assignments plus take-home midterm and final exam over 10 weeks, with mandatory attendance.
grading: 30% homework, 20% attendance/participation, 20% take-home midterm, 30% final exam.
notes: Bridges predictive AI and prescriptive optimization — rare combination in one course.

title: Special Topics: GenAI for Business

offerings.format_notes: Co-taught; includes guest lectures and optional Monday work sessions.

description: A practical course on leveraging Generative AI to create business value: when and how to integrate GenAI into business processes and decision-making. Centerpiece is a quarter- long group project building an 'AI-coworker' prototype that automates a real business process, supported by modules on prompt engineering, RAG, tool use/MCP, and agent systems.
topics: GenAI for data generation and analysis
prerequisites: No programming experience required.
workload_basis: Quarter-long group project with milestones, individual assignments, and weekly TODOs.
grading: 50% group project, 20% individual assignments, 30% participation.
notes: Attendance-sensitive (absent/late more than once lowers participation grade); peer evaluations required.

title: Special Topics: Healthcare Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Compressed 5-week course; missing more than 2 of 5 sessions results in an F.

description: A rigorous introduction to healthcare decision modeling centered on cost-effectiveness analysis for evaluating competing health interventions. Covers deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analysis and Markov cohort and microsimulation models of disease progression, applied to a project on type 2 diabetes medications.
prerequisites: MGTA 453 or knowledge of probability and statistics.
workload_basis: Two homework assignments and a group project over 5 weeks; no exams.
grading: 40% homework, 20% attendance/participation, 40% group project.
notes: Strict mandatory attendance; niche but valuable for healthcare-focused careers.

title: Special Topics: Marketing Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Taught by Head of Analytics at GBK Collective (ex-Bain); no exams.

description: Develops technical, statistical, and communication skills for analytically-based consumer insights. Five topics — experimentation/causal inference, preference measurement via maximum likelihood, conjoint-based pricing with Bayesian methods, segmentation via unsupervised learning, and driver analysis via supervised learning — implemented 'by hand' in code and published as blog posts on a student-built portfolio website.
skills: building a portfolio website with Quarto and Git
workload_basis: Five substantial coding problem sets (~18% each) submitted as website blog posts; no exams; collaboration allowed.
grading: Five assignments ~90%, engagement and website quality ~10%; no exams.
notes: You leave with a public portfolio website of your coursework — a real asset for job searches.

title: Accounting
description: Examines fundamental accounting concepts and principles to help students become informed users of financial statements. Includes interactive lectures, discussions, and short cases involving corporate financial statements to illustrate accounting concepts and explore disclosure strategies.
workload_basis: Graded online homework, class participation, a mid-quarter exam, and a comprehensive final exam.
grading: Graded homework 15%, class participation 10%, mid-quarter exam 25%, and final exam 50%.

title: Investment Analysis
description: This course develops a framework for understanding how investors choose between risky and risk-free securities and construct optimal portfolios. It covers asset pricing models such as CAPM and factor models, fixed income analysis, derivatives, and performance evaluation, with an emphasis on practical implementation using data and cases. Topics also include ESG investing, market efficiency, behavioral finance, private markets, and the use of AI in asset management.
skills: pricing bonds and managing bond portfolios
pricing options using binomial lattice and black-scholes
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes, five assignments, a final exam, and case preparation.
grading: Grades are based on assignments (15%), quizzes (35%), and a final exam (50%).

title: Financial Econometrics and Empirical Methods
description: This course bridges the gap between theoretical financial models and empirical financial econometrics, covering major accomplishments and failures in empirical finance over the last quarter century. Students read seminal works and complete empirical exercises that require writing their own procedures and using real market data.
prerequisites: A quantitatively based “Investments” class is a prerequisite for the course. Familiarity with computers. Students should be able to download and manipulate data. Knowledge of a programming language or statistical package (e.g., Python, Matlab, R) is required. Knowledge of “canned” statistical programs such as Eviews, SAS, or Stata is not enough. Students will be expected to build their own library of routines and procedures from the ground up.
workload_basis: Graded work includes written/computer exercises (40%), weekly quizzes (10%), participation/peer evaluations (10%), and a final examination (40%).
grading: Grading is based on written/computer exercises (40%), weekly quizzes (10%), participation/peer evaluations (10%), and a final examination (40%).

title: Business Forecasting
description: Master of Finance course on forecasting for business and financial decisions: time- series methods, forecast evaluation, and applications to financial and economic data.
skills: building and evaluating forecasting models for finance
prerequisites: Restricted to MFin/MBA or by consent of instructor.
workload_basis: Quantitative MFin coursework; letter grades only.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Pre-approved MSBA elective (MFin course — enrollment by consent). Scheduled for Fall 2026; no Winter or Spring section is on the schedule.

title: Behavioral Finance
description: Master of Finance course on how psychology shapes financial markets and investor behavior: biases, market anomalies, and behavioral explanations for asset-pricing puzzles.
skills: applying behavioral insights to investment and financial decisions
prerequisites: Letter grades only; MFin course.
workload_basis: MFin lecture/case coursework.
grading: See department syllabus.
notes: Pre-approved MSBA elective (MFin course — enrollment by consent). Runs in Spring; no Fall or Winter section is on the schedule.

title: Collecting and Analyzing Financial Data
description: This course teaches students how to obtain and process financial data in order to answer empirical questions in finance. It covers applications in real estate, asset management, private equity, and ESG, with hands-on homework, a group final project, and a final exam. Students use Python-based examples and WRDS data, and may use AI tools for coding syntax.
skills: applying the capm to analyze stock returns
analyzing geographic variation in house prices
using python for financial data analysis
workload_basis: Three homework assignments, a group final project with an 8-minute presentation, and a final exam.
grading: Grades are based on the final presentation (35%), final exam (35%), and three homework assignments (10% each).

title: MQF Professional Seminar
description: A required seminar series for Master of Finance students featuring distinguished leaders from the financial industry. Students attend weekly talks, learn about career paths and current market challenges, and submit team-written summaries reflecting on each session.
workload_basis: Weekly seminar attendance and team-based 1-page summaries submitted after each session.
grading: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory based on attendance and submission of team summaries.

title: Topics in Finance: Preparing for the CFA Exam
description: This course prepares students for the Level 1 CFA exam by covering each of the ten major topic areas tested, including ethics, quantitative methods, financial statement analysis, corporate finance, equity investments, fixed income, derivatives, alternative investments, portfolio management, and economics. Students engage in applied valuation work similar to actual CFA exam questions, use the Bloomberg Terminal, and learn study habits of successful past candidates.
skills: preparing effectively for the cfa level 1 exam
applying the cfa institute code and standards
prerequisites: This class assumes you are a registered CFA level 1 candidate for the 2026 or 2027 exam, and as such will have access to the CFA-required readings.
workload_basis: Weekly reading assignments, weekly in-class quizzes, class participation, and a valuation tournament.
grading: Grades are based on class participation, canvas quizzes, and weekly in-person in-class quizzes, totaling 100 points.

title: Capstone Applied Finance Project
description: Students work in teams on an applied finance project with an industry partner, formulating an empirical question, collecting and analyzing data, and presenting findings. The course emphasizes econometric methods, clear writing, and professional presentation, culminating in a research paper and oral presentations.
skills: presenting technical findings to a professional audience
workload_basis: Graded work includes a 2-page proposal, three team presentations, a 10-page outline, and a final research paper up to 50 pages.
grading: The final grade is determined by the instructors based on the content and style of the research paper and team presentations, with content weighted most.

title: Professional Seminar: Current Topics
description: This course gives students a window into what it is like to be a tax accounting professional in a multinational corporation. It provides a high-level explanation of tax accounting and case law concepts through guest speakers who are senior executives and through study of recent real-life situations affecting the tax accounting profession.
skills: preparing for the far section of the cpa exam
applying accounting topics to real-world examples
identifying earnings manipulation using beneish and sloan models
accounting for nonprofits and government entities
analyzing tax accounts in financial statements
workload_basis: Weekly practice quizzes, homework from Canvas and Becker's Test Bank, and required participation in the equity valuation contest.
grading: Graded on a pass/fail basis based on attendance and participation, including practice quizzes and activities.

title: Business Law
description: This course provides a general understanding of core business law concepts and practical exercises for evaluating how law influences business decision-making. It covers regulation of business actors, contracts, risk creation and mitigation, and resolution of legal disputes. The material also incorporates content tested on the CPA Exam's REG section.
skills: evaluating legal influence on business decisions
workload_basis: Five quizzes (lowest dropped), two group projects plus a smaller project, a final exam, and class participation.
grading: Four quizzes (lowest dropped) count 40%, group work 25%, class participation 10%, and the final exam 25%.

title: Internal Control over Financial Reporting
description: Internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) and its practical application within business processes that produce financial information. The course covers management's and independent auditors' perspectives, including financial reporting assertions, risks of material misstatement, control objectives, control activities, and evaluation of control deficiencies, along with IT controls, governance, fraud risk, and emerging technologies. It is taught from a professional and practical perspective with case studies, guest speakers, group presentations, and documentation exercises.
topics: internal control over financial reporting and coso framework
skills: explaining icfr and the coso framework
analyzing transaction flows through major business processes
identifying financial reporting assertions and risks of material misstatement
evaluating control objectives and control design
documenting processes, risks, and controls with professional tools
explaining the role of it controls and emerging technologies in icfr
communicating icfr analyses and conclusions effectively
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes, speaker advance prep and reflections, group project, and final exam.
grading: The course grade is based on participation/quizzes (30%), speaker advance prep and reflections (10%), group projects (30%), and a final exam (30%).

title: Professional Communications for Accountants
description: This course prepares accounting professionals for job-related oral communication tasks, including formal presentations, informal coworker conversations, and remote communication. Students learn to think purposefully and critically about one-on-one and group communications, tailoring messages to different audiences. The course uses lectures, in-class activities, group discussions, individual speaking assignments, and team projects with constructive feedback.
skills: delivering clear and professional oral presentations
reading and adapting to nonverbal behavior
using digital communication strategies for remote interactions
workload_basis: Graded work includes class participation, individual speaking assignments, team projects, and pre-class assignments.
grading: Class participation counts 15% of the final grade, and all assignments must be completed to pass the course.

title: Professional Research for Accountants
description: Students learn to locate, interpret, and apply authoritative guidance from sources such as the FASB Codification, Internal Revenue Code, PCAOB/AICPA standards, and SEC releases, using professional research platforms including Thomson Reuters Checkpoint Edge and CCH IntelliConnect. The course emphasizes the IRAC framework, professional memo writing, and case-based exercises, and explores the emerging role of artificial intelligence and data analytics in accounting research.
skills: identifying researchable accounting, auditing, and tax issues
navigating the fasb accounting standards codification
applying pcaob and aicpa auditing standards
conducting tax research using primary and secondary authorities
evaluating appropriate uses of artificial intelligence in accounting research
workload_basis: Weekly assignments, in-class participation/exercises/quizzes, and a final research memo.
grading: Graded on weekly assignments (40%), in-class participation, exercises and quizzes (20%), and a final research memo (40%).

title: Advanced Auditing & Forensic Accounting
description: A graduate-level, applied treatment of the financial statement assurance function, emphasizing audit judgment, evidence evaluation, data analytics, and forensic accounting. Students conduct a staged audit engagement across the quarter, investigate a real fraud enforcement case, and complete CPA-format checks aligned with the AUD exam.
skills: evaluating client acceptance and engagement risk
testing internal controls and evaluating deficiencies
executing substantive procedures using audit data analytics
workload_basis: Weekly prep bundles, five audit simulation installments, an individual data analytics deliverable, a fraud autopsy project, a midterm, and a mock CPA check; estimated 6 out-of-class hours per week.
grading: Graded on weekly prep bundles (10%), participation (10%), audit simulation (30%), individual data analytics deliverable (10%), mock AUD check (5%), fraud autopsy project (10%), and midterm exam (25%).

title: Global Taxation and Business Strategy
description: Examines the foundations of corporate international tax strategies for US multinational corporations, including the tax economics of corporate formations, operations, reorganizations, liquidations, and entity classification. Covers US and international jurisdictional tax topics that support effective business decisions and help reduce risk while increasing after-tax cash flows. Taught through lectures, readings, discussion problems, quizzes, and a final exam.
topics: hybrid transactions and tax rate arbitrage
skills: identifying international tax issues in corporate structuring
analyzing tax consequences of entity classification
applying us international tax rules to multinational operations
evaluating transfer pricing and cost sharing arrangements
comparing pre- and post-2017 international tax planning
calculating tax accounting for property and corporate transactions
assessing global tax initiatives' impact on business strategy
workload_basis: Weekly readings, discussion problem sets, quizzes, a final discussion problem, and a final exam.
grading: Grading is based on attendance (10%), participation in in-class problems (25%), quizzes (25%), a final discussion problem (10%), and a final exam (25%).
